statement: With L1 assumptions and D_n(K)=sum_{k<=K} k a_{n,k}, Var(M_n)<=D_n(K)+n/(K+1) and D_n(K)<=K Var(M_n). A bound D_n(floor n^a)<=C n^(1-b), a,b>0, implies Var(M_n)<=(C+1)n^(1-min(a,b)); a variance power epsilon implies spectral escape at cutoff n^(epsilon/2) with exponent epsilon/2.
assumptions: a,b>0 for the conditional power consequence
all stated asymptotic hypotheses hold uniformly for large n

statement: For n>=2,m>=8, the maximum T_{n,m} of n-vertex paths on a root with m disjoint Gaussian corridors has gradient squared norm n, every nonroot vertex influence 1/m, and 1+c(n-1)/log(2m)<=Var(T_{n,m})<=1+2(n-1)/log m for absolute c>0. Hence m=n refutes a generic small-influence-to-polynomial-variance inference, without refuting the actual quadrant-lattice C0120 target.
assumptions: a common root and m disjoint corridors of n-1 further vertices
all paths consist of the root and exactly one full corridor
standard Gaussian hypercontractivity for the upper bound; elementary Mills bounds suffice for the obstruction
